newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: DHL to spend $2 mln to expand Bahrain hub.
newsitem.headline: DHL to spend $2 mln to expand Bahrain hub.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express is to spend 750,000 dinars ($2 million) expanding its Middle East regional distribution centre in Bahrain, chairman Patrick Lupo said.
In a statement, Lupo said throughput at the facility has risen to 1,400 tonnes a month from 500 tonnes in November 1993, when the facility opened.

"This increase, together with the introduction of the daily Boeing B757 freighter service, has necessitated adding approximately 20,000 square feet of warehouse space to process the heavy door-to-door airfreight," the statement said.
The complex is currently about 40,000 square feet.
Lupo said the expansion was part of DHL's 1993 plan to spend $65 million over five years to develop its infrastructure in the region.
Construction was expected to start in January and should be completed in August 1997. Some 25 new Bahraini jobs would be created during the first year of operation, he said.
Regional hub and transportation director Geoff Kehr said a new EDI customs clearance system was being used at the Bahrain centre.
Lupo said DHL was in talks to build airside facilities -- similar to those in Bahrain, Dubai and Cairo -- in Abu Dhabi, Doha, Kuwait, Riyadh, Jeddah and in Pakistan.
The main shareholders in DHL Worldwide Express are Deutsche Lufthansa AG and Japan Airlines Co Ltd. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
